ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #16
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a describing word
   B. Only an action
   C. A person, place, thing, or idea
   D. Only a joining word

2. When practising Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.

3. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.

4. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

5. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.

6. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.

7. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goes
   B. goed
   C. going
   D. went

8. When practising Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks.

9. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.

10. When practising Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.

11. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. where is the library
   B. Where is the Library
   C. Where is the library
   D. Where is the library?

12. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Only one word repeated
   B. Many unrelated topics with no link
   C. One main idea with supporting sentences
   D. No full stops

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Narrative Composition 10.5.1 Packing and Shopping lists 11.5.1 Spelling Antonyms and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 9.5.1 Creative writing: Narrative compositions and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 10.1.1 Oral Presentations: Delivering Speeches and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Oral Presentations: Delivering Speeches and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — A person, place, thing, or idea

2. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.

3. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.

4. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

5. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.

6. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.

7. D — went

8. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks.

9. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.

10. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.

11. D — Where is the library?

12. C — One main idea with supporting sentences

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Narrative Composition 10.5.1 Packing and Shopping lists 11.5.1 Spelling Antonyms; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Writing 9.5.1 Creative writing: Narrative compositions; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening and Speaking 10.1.1 Oral Presentations: Delivering Speeches; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Oral Presentations: Delivering Speeches; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
